utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. I was told that you, Mr. McCloskey, good morning, have -- want to raise some matters. Please do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours, everyone. Yes, I just wanted to remind the Court of a meeting we all had, the parties all had, not long ago, a few days ago, where I promised to provide everyone with some paper indicating the witnesses that would be called and estimates on remaining time. That's almost ready. As soon as we can give Ms. Stewart a few minutes out of court, she will just check a few of our numbers and get that out today. Just very briefly I can tell you thus far we have had 78 trial days and we've put on 49 witnesses. We have 87 witnesses to go: 25 of those are full viva voce; 21, 92 ter; 41, basically, 92 bis with cross, so the same as 92 ter. And we have endeavoured to revise our own estimates based on what we see ourselves doing with - especially with these 92 ter witnesses - anticipating some of your questions and what we have learned about General Tolimir's time that he has taken, and I think I would guess I'm speaking for everyone that all parties have appreciated the time you've allowed us to do this work and to put on our witnesses, including, even, re-cross, which in my system that I barely remember now is something that is appropriate in some circumstances, like you have found. So that's much appreciated. Though that does, when you start getting realistic, does tend to, well, certainly takes it beyond my initial thoughtful idea of June, which was even before the 92 bis, before I'd factored in the 92 bis ruling. The other thing to point out is, we are really coming to some of the most significant witnesses, and these will be VRS witnesses, Serbian MUP witnesses, high-level people that we can now see that the General will probably take a fair amount of time with putting on his case and that you will be, of course, very interested in. And so it now looks more like beyond the summer break of 2011, and Mr. Thayer is thinking it's more like October or November. But I want you to see those figures, see the remaining witnesses, and if then -- of course, we're open for any rulings, discussions, debates, criticisms on those, but we did our best to be more realistic based on what we're seeing happen in court. And I think our -- thus far, our 78 -- well, the trial days we've put in has -- have -- I don't think anyone's wasted any time. I think they've been a good pace. I think anyone watching should have felt that. Of course, early on we couldn't put in four days a week four understandable reasons. Now we're doing four days a week, and so we're basing that on a four-day-a-week with the vacations and the summer breaks and everything involved, so ... And one last comment on these significant VRS and Serb MUP witnesses based on some of the questions the other day, it has always been the case in this trial, and actually in many other trials, that many of these witnesses we put on to you and they will not be telling the whole story. They will be -- have involved in the events themselves, they will not be telling you the whole story, and in many cases they will be outright lying to you. That is understood by us, and we will be questioning them on direct and redirect, and we believe that you will be able to sort out the differences between the truth and the lie and the significant points and look to the corroboration, but it will be a -- well, an exciting and difficult job, as it always is, but that's the expectation we have for many of those witnesses, so ... And having said that, we're ready for Ms. Gallagher who will continue going through the trial video and our stills book in what I know will make much more sense as I think even the witness testimony yesterday, as we heard the descriptions of the territory that I think must have sounded very familiar to you. So we're ready to go with that. But as a reminder, what she is going over is the material that has been originally developed for this case, video material and still-book material. We have since obtained some new material, so when she's done with this first chapter, she will come back again for chapter 2 of some more video - not a whole lot more, but some more video - some of which you've seen, some of which you've not seen, to give you the final chapter of video. But when she's done with this first segment, we'll be able to give you DVDs of these -- of the video -- well, it should be in evidence, I hope, at that point, so we'll be able to give you the DVDs so everybody has what has been shown fully, so it's -- so you have easy access to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. McCloskey, indeed. It's a very difficult situation in a certain way disappointing that we have to go for such a long time, your time estimation. We have to consider the situation, and, of course, we have to ensure that we will have a fair but also an expeditious trial. And we have to discuss, for instance, if we could sit five days a week, if we could have longer sitting times per day, if we reduce the time available for the parties. All these matters or measures should be taken into account by the Chamber and the parties. But I don't want to comment on that now because we have to consider your information you were able to give us. At this point in time, I would like to ask Mr. Tolimir if he has some comments on that and if you could perhaps indicate if there will be a Defence case, if you intend to call witnesses, Defence witnesses, and if so, perhaps how many. It's not necessary that you give us this information now, but you will understand that we need a kind of estimation about the length of the whole trial. Is it possible for you to give us some additional information?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no comments with regard to what Mr. McCloskey has just stated. I would like to thank you for the organisation and the efforts in helping him present his case so far. I will be able to give you the number of witnesses and my estimate only when I am fully aware what the Prosecution has and what they say. We are not going to take witnesses just to take witnesses, but for the facts and for the events. I wouldn't be able to inform you about the number of witnesses now. In any case, we will need much less time than the Prosecutor, twice as little as the Prosecutor I would say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. There's no need for further discussion of this. We will take all information into account. The witness should be brought in, please. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Ms. Stewart will be running the trial video which is P991. The transcript is P1008. And the stills that she'll be going over that are on e-court are from Exhibit P624, and I have the e-court page numbers for you when we get to those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Gallagher. Please sit down. Welcome to the courtroom again. We are still in the phase of examination-in-chief, and I would like to remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth you made at the beginning of your testimony still applies. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Right. And if it helps, we finished up on the 29th of September, and we had played up to 14.53.2 on the trial video. And now we're starting at a place called Potocari, 11 July, Dutch Battalion soldier footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Ms. Gallagher - good morning - what that is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning. It's -- you'll see footage of refugees from Srebrenica being brought in on trucks, massive groups of people loaded onto the trucks, being driven in - and they're UN trucks - being driven in to the UN base in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did we get that footage?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's footage that we got from Antelope Productions, and that was the independent production company that made a documentary called "A Cry From the Grave." And this footage they received from a DutchBat warrant officer who had done the videotaping in Potocari at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did they give us his name?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: His same a Wim Dijkema.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And I think we can just play that -- play that footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Ms. Gallagher, we're at 0016.36.9. I don't want to ask you anything particular about this shot except that can you tell us whether or not this footage we're seeing from the Dutch soldier, was this edited by the Prosecution to -- or are we getting all the video that the Dutch soldier took?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pertaining to the people coming in to -- the women and children, elderly and sick being brought into Potocari, I am aware that this is the full footage of this particular section.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. We're now at 18.36.5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Correct me if I'm wrong, I thought there had been some editing of that Potocari footage, can you -- do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I do -- you do notice that there's -- there's quite a bit of edits. I think some of that may be from the videotaper stopping the footage at the time. I would have to actually -- would want to confirm how much of or if any of that was editing by Marta Fracassetti for the purposes of the trial video. My recollection is as most of what was in the footage of coming into Potocari was in here, but I would want to double-check that for you, because I do see a fair number of edits.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And as the Court knows, you'll be back for part two of this for the new video that is going to go into the trial video and new still book, so we'll mark that down as a check. All right. Now we're at, what is entitled on the trial video, "Mladic and Others Approach and Enter Srebrenica."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you go on with this, Judge Nyambe has a question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you. Just now in answer to Mr. McCloskey's question, you've said "because I do see a fair number of edits." How are you able to identify where the footage is edited or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When you watch it you'll see a jump from one scene to the next scene, it will be very, very quick but you can see that it's not being played all throughout in its entirety. It will move to, let's say, another viewpoint of the people coming off the trucks. So watching it closely, you will see that there's a slight jump. Sometimes what's difficult to tell is that -- is that -- the jump of the videographer who's just stopped and the videotape has gone and moved and then proceeded to videotape more, or if it's an edit from our editor here, putting footage together and taking some of -- you know, taking some of it out and editing with other footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. We see title of this next segment, we see: "Antelope Reuters SRT footage." And you've told us about Antelope Productions, the people that did "Cry From the Grave." We know that Reuters is a news agency. And SRT, can you remind us what that is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's "Srpska Radio Television."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's -- let's play that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in the -- can we go to, in P6 - there we go - P624, e-court page 9. All right. I think if we can blow that up a little bit, I can't -- I don't know about anybody else, but I'm having a hard time reading that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So can you just go over the numbers, just to remind us who these folks are?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: So starting with number 1 is the body-guard of General Ratko Mladic, who we do know his identity now, it's Branislav Puhalo; number 2 is General Radislav Krstic, chief of staff of the Drina Corps; three is General Ratko Mladic, commander of the VRS; and four is Colonel Vinko Pandurevic, commander of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And we soon see -- and we've seen a little bit of a person with a blue helmet, and we'll see that. Has the investigation come to any kind of conclusion on whether that person with a blue helmet was a DutchBat or VRS?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is not a DutchBat member. It's a VRS soldier. And you'll see that General Mladic will ask him to put on the blue helmet and get into the tank to look like they are helping UNPROFOR at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So how do you know it's VRS? Or why do you think that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In, actually, a statement by Drazan Ademovic, he identifies who several of the people are, the 10th Sabotage Unit members. And also you will hear General Mladic speaking to him in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's just continue to play the -- the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Let me ask, I don't see a blue helmet. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yeah, that was my preview of the coming attraction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Oh, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We -- we saw a bit of it, but you couldn't see it very well. But it should be the next few seconds, if I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- if I'm correct. That was just to get you ready for something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we're starting at 20.33.0.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we are at 21.54.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you just point out if you see the blue helmet?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see the person with the blue helmet up top of the APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did we see him just -- just prior to this when Mladic said something like, "Show how we're helping"?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. At 23.16.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you just remind us where the investigation believes this is happening, where they're coming down this little road, just roughly?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure. It's the approach into Srebrenica. And, actually, Vinko Pandurevic had viewed this footage when he testified in January 2009 and pointed out he believed this to be the Bojna area, which is south of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Roughly how many kilometres?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would guess around 5, maybe a little bit less. Less than 5 possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. We can -- let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. We are at 24.08.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: They've just, we've seen, come into an area of vehicles and buildings. Can you tell us roughly where this is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the southern part of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We're at 25.04.3. Can we go to page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: 25.04.3. We're at page 11 in the e-court stills book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we see, again, number 1 is Radislav Krstic, who I think we're all beginning to recognise. How about number -- number 2?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 2, as you see, is Velimir Popovic, aka Vela, and also number 3; they're both members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment. And, if I can go ahead, number 3 is Stanko Savanovic, also a member of the 10th Sabotage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how do we know that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were both identified by Drazen Erdemovic, both in the Popovic trial and also recently in the Perisic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And it says "down-town Srebrenica, 11 July"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I think we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. This is number 14 in the stills book, at 25.43.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, again, I'm sure we recognise General Mladic, and that's number 2. And number 1 is Milenko Zivanovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We know that through the course of the investigation. He is a familiar face, just like General Krstic, General Mladic. We've seen him on multiple videos, multiple interviews, as you'll see in the course of the rest of the video. And he's -- and I think he may have originally been identified by investigator Jean-Rene Ruez earlier on in earlier trials.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And is he referred to in some nickname that you recall in these -- in this video and other places?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zile.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's Z-i-l-e?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And you might need to slow your speech a little bit, if you can. I imagine that -- and I'll try to delay a bit myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I think we can continue to play the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now could we go to page -- 25.46.5, at page 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, we can see that it says here: "General Mladic and Members of the Drina Wolves of the Zvornik Brigade." And how were you able -- the team able to identify them as -- and who, as Drina Wolves?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You'll see the two men with the arm patches and the red ribbons on their arms, those are two Drina Wolves members. We don't know who they are specifically, but the arm patch is very specific to the Drina Wolves unit. And in the prior footage, you saw that Legenda, Milan Jolovic, was the commander of the Drina Wolves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Here at 27.57.0, just before that we heard General Mladic speak to Krle, K-r-l-e. Who is that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the nickname for General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You'll also see in much -- in much footage him refer to him as Krle, and other footage you'll see him call him Krle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We are at 28.38.1, that is page 13. There you go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, this says, and since it's in English, I'll just -- it's Colonel Mirko Trivic, commander of the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade, Drina Corps, it said he identified himself at trial; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. He identified himself in the Popovic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did he command units of his brigade in the attack on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. He was commander of the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then we see the next, number 2, is identified as Milan Tupajic --

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tupajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- president of the Municipal Assembly of Sokolac, that he was identified by Trivic at trial, and by General Krstic at his trial. And is that also correct in your double-checking these?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Krstic -- General Krstic identified him in the year 2000 in his trial and Colonel Trivic in the Popovic in - if I can check - May 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I think we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We are at 28.52.4. That's number 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I think at this point we certainly recognise General Mladic and General Zivanovic. We now see number 1, the woman, as Dana Bartula. And was she a member of the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And identified by her commander, Mirko Trivic?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I think we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We're at 30.35.6, number 19 on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I note that we see the back of number 2's head, but -- and identify him as Zivanovic. Were you able to, in looking at the entire video, see his face in this sequence?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He turns around. You see that it's General Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, number 1, who is that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel Vujadin Popovic, chief of security for the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is also a familiar face to us over the course of the investigation and over the trial of the Popovic et al. trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We just saw a rather significant statement for the Prosecution. And if the Court -- we'll see that, and Ms. Stewart will play that one more time because you may recall, it starts out with a certain sort of clarity as he's speaking, and then after he says, "We'll give this as a gift," it switches into a whole 'nother kind of clarity, and he goes on and makes the comment about the Dahis and take revenge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you -- and I will go back to your initial explanation of how Ms. Fracassetti edited the various materials trying to find the best quality and editing where things were cut out. So could you explain what happened, if anything, in the -- in -- as Ms. Fracassetti, where you edited this particular part. And first of all, have you had a chance recently to speak Ms. Fracassetti about this particular part precisely?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A few weeks ago I did speak with Marta Fracassetti and asked her specifically about this segment, because as you noticed, it's two sources of video footage edited together. And what she had told me at that time is, as I mentioned before, she always tries to use the best quality footage possible. And you will see the nice quality, very clear sound and video, prior. And that is all the footage that she got from that source, which was from Antelope Productions. The Tribunal also received other footage from, that you see, from SRT, Srpska Radio Television, of this same interview. And it is the exact same interview except for there's this last little bit that's included, which was not a part of what we received from Antelope Productions. So what she did is use the best-quality footage, as much as she could from the Antelope footage, and -- but it was not complete, and so then added in the SRT footage to make it the complete interview that he -- he did on July 11th, in the centre of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we all know that video is just a series of frames all put together. Did you ask Ms. Fracassetti if she -- if there was any frames missing in this interview that she couldn't link?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. She was able to absolutely line up the -- both footages so then it was seamless link from what finished of the Antelope, the nice quality footage, and then immediately just connected it with the SRT footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we'll just play that segment over again so you can try to get a picture of what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And as a reminder, we start with Antelope; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's the good quality?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then Antelope actually stopped. It didn't have the complete footage; correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But the Serb TV, that was published on the TV, did?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And -- all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so we're starting again at 30.37.7, where Antelope is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now I wanted to see if we can -- we tried to, in preparation, a couple of weeks ago, we are a little rusty on this. I believe we're going to try to play the segment of Antelope that we had, so you can see the segment of Antelope, and the segment of the RS TV so you can see the two segments that Ms. Fracassetti put together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to be starting with the -- is this Antelope or Serb TV?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Serb TV there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So we're going to start with the -- the complete -- the version we got from Serb TV. Okay. Go ahead, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And that little segment of Serb TV we have numbered 6597, and for the record we just ended it at 00.31.8.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, so that was the complete interview. Of course, it was not subtitled because it was not the finished product, I take it?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But -- so that, on Serb TV, was the complete little interview where he's talking about giving it as a gift and then as revenge?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the next segment we'll see, which is -- just a minute. This should be the -- it should be from P681 times 12.40 to 13.03 which should be the Antelope section.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So that was the -- the complete version of the Antelope footage that we got that's the high quality?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But, of course, it was missing the key part.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so Ms. Fracassetti took the good-quality Antelope and the poor quality and, where they overlapped, joined them together. Is that a simple way of saying it?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did she do that, you know, throughout these sections where similar things occurred?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I think we can - there's no questions - just continue to go forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We are stopped at 31.13.6. Could we go to page 15 in the still book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, again, we are now, I hope, familiar with General Krstic, is number 1; General -- at that time Colonel Pandurevic at number 3; Mladic, of course; and Lieutenant-Colonel Vujadin Popovic at number 2. Did you have any trouble identifying him in this, what is a little -- well, blurry on the picture, not quite as blurry on the video?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you saw him a few minutes earlier. And in another photograph it's obviously the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: 31.28.7, page 16 in the stills book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We have a new -- a new face, Colonel Svetozar Andric, commander of the 1st Birac, or known as the Sekovici Infantry Brigade of the Drina Corps. Identified by Mr. Ruez. Have you been able to confirm that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware that. Jean-Rene Ruez actually interviewed Svetozar Andric himself in 2000. And also I confirmed that Vinko Pandurevic identified him in -- himself in his own trial in January 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did Colonel Andric's units take part in the attack on the enclave?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we see, in what is a bit blurry on this photograph, that number 2 has been identified as Lieutenant Milorad Pelemis, commander of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, a unit of the Main Staff of VRS. Is that all correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And it says he was identified by Drazen Erdemovic in one of his interviews; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And would Pelemis have been the commander of Drazen Erdemovic?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just to remind the Court, where was Drazen Erdemovic and his unit on the 16th of July or some of his unit on 16 July?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th of July, they participated in the execution at Branjevo farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And according to Erdemovic, was Pelemis at that execution, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Just for Your Honours, I think for all sides, that it's clear that there's never been any evidence that Milorad Pelemis was at the -- was at that execution, and you'll see the evidence in the record. Okay. I think we can continue. If we could have one moment. We've come to the Hotel Fontana segments, which, as I'm sure you will recall, you have seen two of the three meetings with a very recent Muslim witness, so we won't play those for you again. They're a bit lengthy. You saw the second meeting at 11.00 between the Muslim representative and DutchBat and Mladic, and then you saw the morning of the 12th, the 10.00 meeting, with more Muslim representatives and a large group. You have not recently seen the first Hotel Fontana meeting at about 8.00 on 11 July, but our witness next week was at that particular meeting, a Dutch soldier, so we will play it with him as opposed to you seeing that now and then seeing it again. So if we could just have a minute with -- Ms. Stewart and I will be able to adjust. Okay. Now we're going at 1.54.00.0. And it's the segment entitled "Potocari, 12 July 1995," from Reuters and Serb television. And I think we can just play that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We are at 1.54.13.4, at page 42 of the stills book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this is a -- four men that have been identified. The first one, Milan Milinkovic, known as Like, member of the 2nd Battalion, 1st Company of the Bratunac Brigade. He identified himself in an OTP interview on 18 January. Is that correct and confirmed by you?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I've read the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you, perhaps, tell us who took this interview, who was the OTP representative?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in 2003 and ... yeah, I -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can get a list of homework going on that. So I think, if it's okay, she can check that at the break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, it was one of the OTP investigators on the Srebrenica team, but at the moment I have forgotten who did the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, number 2 is Dobrisav Stanojevic, known as Miko, and it says he's a member of the 1st Company of the Separate Police Unit, known as PJP, of the CJB Zvornik MUP. And then there's -- number 3 is Dusan Micic, who is also a PJP member but from the same unit. And number 4, Radenko Tomic, known as Gargija, a member of Mauzer's Panthers Unit of the East Bosnia Corps. And we see, at number 4, that Radenko Tomic had identified himself in an OTP interview on 15 March 2001 and 18 January 2003. Do you know which investigator, do you recall there?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I know Bruce Bursik did a number of the interviews in 2003, but I've read so many of them I actually can't remember if he exact -- if he did both of these.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But were these, as you say, all Srebrenica team members that were actually doing this?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And then we see all identified by Dobrisav Stanojevic at trial. And Dobrisav is number 2. Which trial was that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in Popovic. And he -- he identified them in June of 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, of course, this photo, we see number 1, we can hardly see him, let alone his face; number 2 is his back; number 3 is his back; and we do get a look, somewhat blurry look, at number 4. Can you explain, were these identifications made from this still or from something else?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they're made from the video. So you'll see -- you'll see them, in the video, walk through, and you'll see them a little bit later. You'll see number 4 later, you'll see number 2 later. So they're not being identified just by their -- the back of their heads.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you remember how many of these guys had bandanas on?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's two different ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that would be who?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like, number one. And also number 4, Radenko Tomic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I think we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go -- 1.54.27.2. Let's go to page 43.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, here we get a very nice shot of one fellow in a bandana identified as Milan Milinkovic or Like. And has that all been confirmed by you?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So this is, number 1, the fellow that we could barely see in that last one?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... 1.55.10.6.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. McCloskey kindly speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'll get there. 1.55.10.6. And this is page 45.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, this is noted to be Dobrisav Stanojevic who was number 2 in that first one we saw, with his back to the group. But this identifies him as -- again, as a member of a PJP, or a police unit, and that he identified himself at trial. Now, which -- which trial?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, the Popovic trial. And that was in June 2007 when he identified himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And he's the fellow that identified those -- those other folks --

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- at the same trial? Now, we see at location at the bottom, Potocari, outside of the "White House," 12 July 1995. First of all, how -- how have you determined this was at 12 July?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partly due to the content that -- that, as you'll see, it's when the refugees are leaving, being put on buses, as well as the statements and testimony of those that were there and stated that it was on July 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And how do you know that it was outside of the "White House," have you been to this area?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have. I recognise where the area is. You see the UN base in the background. The -- there's a small road, that they're entering onto the main road. I recognise that. You'll see more footage where you'll see that it is the "White House" right to the right, as we're looking at Dobrisav Stanojevic there, right to the right side of him as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I think we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This isn't a great shot, and I don't see him in the still book, but do you recall, is this -- is this one of the people we've seen before, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe he's the one that we saw earlier, Gargija.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So there's -- Gargija and Like are the two people with the bandanas?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you remember Gargija's name?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radenko Tomic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And how you know that's Radenko Tomic?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was identified by Dobrisav Stanojevic in trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I think we can -- and that -- this still a 1.55.36.6. I think we can continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And I'm sorry, if I can also add that he identified himself in an interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We have stopped it at 01.56.24.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I just stopped it there to ask you, has the investigation over the years made any effort to try to identify any of these refugee or Muslim faces in the crowd?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The team has, over the years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And has a book been developed of those identifications?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it has.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you will be testifying about that book when we -- when we need you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I think we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know where this footage came from, these pans?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we're at 1.57.09.5.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We got this footage from the BBC. BBC got the footage from WTN and Reuters. And presumably they got the footage from the people that were there filming. There are both some civilians, as you saw, from SRT, some journalists that were there, as well as those attached to the military that were also videotaping.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So we can't narrow it down to an individual in this particular case?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we see, on this still, the Dutch lined up across the road, and we see the buses in the -- some -- well, I know they're buses, but are those buses that we see back there?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yeah. It's near the bus compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you recognise, you know, where this is in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. As I said, it's near the bus compound, just 50, 100 metres up from the -- the "White House".

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can that be confirmed to be on -- on 12 or 13 July?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this to be on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And does the investigation have aerial images that show the bus compound and where people were relative to it on the 12th and 13th July?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I won't ask you anything more about that, but let's continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you stop for a moment, please. Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: I just want a clarification. Just now you said: "Can that be confirmed to be on the 12th or 13th of July?" And you say: "I believe this to be on the" - I think you said - "12th of July." How are you able to tell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The -- all the BBC footage that you see in this section is -- is -- seems to be from the same time-frame of July 12th in -- both with the content of what's happening but once again also with witnesses that have testified or made statements that they were there on July 12th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This, in fact, is a correction of the transcript: At page 26, line 7, where it is said that it was on the 1st of July, it should be the 12th. Thank you. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We are at 1.57.29.9, but let's go to the still of that rough time-frame, which is number 46.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this is identified, this number 1, as Ljubomir Borovcanin, the deputy commander of the Special Police brigade of the MUP. And it says he identified himself in an OTP interview of 20 February 2002. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. He was interviewed by Allistair Graham, investigator on the Srebrenica team, in 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And has there been other -- other people that have identified him over the years?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And many people, including myself, that have identified him over the years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And what about the date, has that been confirmed or -- in his interview, or ...

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, on July 12th, he's in front of this area handing out candy to the children.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I think we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We are at 1.58.32.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we've gone through this once before, but just -- can you tell us -- can you identify the two people in the blue helmets?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who the man in the left is that were -- with the UN blue helmet. I -- obviously, I'm presuming a UN - perhaps a DutchBat, but I don't know for sure - member. And from this angle, I can't see very well with the glasses if that perhaps is Colonel Kingori. I -- it's a little hard to see from this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's just continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We are at 1.59.31.5. And let's go to page 47.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, number 1 is a distinctive fellow with sunglasses and a moustache that you may recall seeing him in the immediate video before this, and he is said to have identified himself in an OTP interview on 18 October 2000, and he was the assistant commander for training of the Special Police brigade of the Jahorina training centre, MUP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And was he a subordinate of Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he reported directly to Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And number 2, who was identified by Dusko Jevic on that -- in that interview, is Dragan Vasiljevic. Is that correct and confirmed?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how did you confirm these -- I think we see number 6, is that the person you've named now?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, Branislav Puhalo, body-guard for General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And 4 and 5, also identified as body-guards, how did you identify them as body-guards?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's -- it's -- I think, originally, it was identified by investigator Jean-Rene Ruez, however you will see them throughout the course of almost all the footage. They are with General Mladic throughout the entire Srebrenica operation. You'll see many other videos with them acting as security with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, I believe it's break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed. We must have the first break now, and we will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey, just one observation. We have seen many of these videos already. It's only a question of use of time. You should be aware of the length of the examination-in-chief of this witness. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I'll incorporate that into the presentation, if I -- especially as I see videos come up. So I think we can -- let's continue and see where this gets us. I think we've already dealt with this particular still, so I think we can continue the video. Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Taking your advice, we'll skip through this material. And there is an interview with General Krstic which may be a little less familiar to you that I think we can start with. It's very, very brief, in Potocari, at the same point. But I think we've seen General Mladic a few times and the Dutch and Kingori and all, so I think that is a good idea, especially since you've suggested it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. We are at 2.03.06.0.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you tell us what we're about to see?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You'll see an interview of a journalist, I believe an SRT journalist, who is interviewing General Krstic about the Srebrenica operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what date does this interview take place?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: July 12th, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Krstic himself testified in his own trial. And you will, in some upcoming photographs, see others that also testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when he testified, did he testify under oath with cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I think we can play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We are now at 02.04.05.9. And could we go to page 49, which reflects this same shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we see that number 1 is Dalibor Krstic, the driver of General Krstic. Of course, there's -- number 2 is Radislav Krstic, and 3 is Vujadin Popovic. And it states that all three of these individuals were identified by General Krstic at his own trial. And is that correct and confirmed by you?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, he identified them on October 30th, 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I think we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we go to page 50. But before we do that, 02.04.24.9 is where we are now. And now page 50. And could we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in public session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. If we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And we're stopping -- that's a tricky one. I think that's close enough. Let's go to -- we're at -- sorry, you are very good, and I appreciate it. 02.04.26.1. And now we can go to number 51.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where we get a better -- a little better still of what Mr. -- almost got. Number 1, Zoran Kovacevic, commander of the 4th Company of the 2nd Battalion Bratunac Brigade. We see how he was identified, he's giving an interview. Is that confirmed?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can we go down a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now we have number 2, this distinctive fellow with the bald head and the big mustache, identified: Lieutenant-Colonel Svetozar Kosoric, chief of intelligence of the Drina Corps. But there is nothing in the document saying how that was come to. How do you or the investigation know that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, from the footage that was in Hotel Fontana, he was identified there by Colonel Boering, so I think that was the first time that he was identified in this book. And in the video, I am also familiar with who he is from numerous video footage over the years, and I can identify him as Svetozar Kosoric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And let's go down to the bottom of the page for the location. We see it says "Potocari, plus or minus 200 metres south of the UN base, 12 July." How do you know, first of all, the location where this was?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just from the video footage. You'll see roughly the location as being further south from the UN base.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So were you able to recognise those bits and pieces of buildings you see by -- as the vehicles are passing?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I roughly recognise the area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how do you know it's 12 July?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, it's from statements and testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We are at 2.04.48.3. And can we go to 52.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We see this is a -- person number 1 is Rade Micic, a member of the 2nd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade, identified by Brano Ilic in an OTP interview. Can you tell us who Brano Ilic is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a member of the 2nd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade. You'll see him coming up a little bit later in the footage. He's in the footage himself, so he identifies himself, he identifies a number of other people. He also has -- has played -- I've met him myself, he's played a role in managing the Hotel Fontana since it closed down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I think we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Here we are at 02.05.09.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And it just -- it said, before that, "a broadcast." Can you tell us what this -- what this is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a daily news, broadcasted on SRT; and it, as you see, the date is July 12th, 1995, and he -- you'll see momentarily, he interviews Radoslav [sic] Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So Radovan Karadzic. And when you say "date," we see that right above the Cyrillic, I guess. It's a bit hard to see it. I think it's written across South America "12.7.1995"?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I interrupt you. Witness, you said "Radoslav Karadzic," and it's recorded that way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I'd like to correct that. It's "Radovan Karadzic." I had "Radislav Krstic" in my head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I think we can play that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is, I believe, four or five minutes. Would you like to hear it or would you like to skip over it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I don't recall having seen that already in this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't either. And I'm not sure if we played it with Mr. Ruez, so it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- a significant piece, so ... thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We should stop for a moment. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. From the very beginning, I've not had the sound in the interview given by President Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps you should move to channel 4. This is the English channel. We could hear the Serbian language used by the speakers, but there's, of course, no translation from Serbian to B/C/S. Perhaps this is the way to deal with that. Shall we start from the beginning again?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. From the very beginning Karadzic speaks Serbian. I can't hear anything. The tone has been completely lowered. I can only see the subtitles. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Again, you should try to go to channel 4. Because it's -- we heard the original voice on channel 4. Let's start again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I hope you were able to follow in the Serbian language. Did you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. I was able to follow on channel 4, just as you instructed me to do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher, we're at 02.12.41.8. This is -- we have this as Reuters footage of 12 July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how do you -- again, do you know this is 12 July?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's from statements of some of the members that were there from the Bratunac Brigade, that they were in Potocari on the 12th for a short time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could now go to page 60.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Have you reviewed page 60 through 63 in this book?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And are these various identifications of Bratunac Brigade and PJP members?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And are they correctly identified and the sources correctly identified?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would intend to go through these stills very quickly because these are very particular identifications of Bratunac Brigade members that I think is important for this trial. It was mainly very important for the trial of the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, which is while [sic] it's here, but unless anyone want us to go over these individually, I think they speak for themselves, and she has just testified that they are accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: How many more of these stills do you have prepared?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There are -- well, of the stills of these Bratunac Brigade and MUP soldiers, they're all very similar and there's several of them. There's -- there's four pages that I would go through very quickly just to have her confirm them, because they will be in the book that you will get.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, I think this is a good way to deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this -- can you tell us where this is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, it's in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And let's go to the next page, 61.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And are these identifications correct and is -- it's basically in the same place?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. They came in as a group together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you know how far away this section of the street is, roughly, from the UN compound?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's on the other side of the street, right near the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 62 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And are these accurate, and is this in the same place?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: On the same date, 12 July?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And 63.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And are the -- same place, same date, correct IDs?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, I'm not sure if Ms. Stewart can find this next section. It's a little bit different. So if we could go to page 64 right now just to see the still that we're getting to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I think we'll first talk about the still. We see a bus with Muslim women and children getting on it. Where is this happening?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's also in Potocari. It's in a nearby location --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- as the other stills.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we see that two soldiers have been identified as Bratunac Brigade. One is Radenko Zaric of the Bratunac Brigade military police. Is that identification correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Milovan Mitrovic, again, Bratunac Brigade military police?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you make out in Zaric's hand, when you watch the video, can you tell what's -- what are in his -- both his hands, aside from hold -- cradling that rifle?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a pencil and paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And I think we can just play that section of the footage. We are at -- we're starting at 02.13.04.0.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We are at 02.13.15.5. Can we go to page 65.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And is this a correct ID of -- all we have is that he's a member of the Special Police brigade of the Jahorina training centre identified by Dusko Jevic? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Dusko Jevic identified him as part of the deserter unit of the Special Police brigade, Jahorina unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, again, remind us, Dusko Jevic, did he have any command authority over that unit?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the direct commander of the Jahorina training centre of the deserter units and reported directly to Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I think we can continue the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. If we could stop right there for a second. We're at 02.13.19.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us, it says "Luke." Where's that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's on the way towards Kladanj. It's near Tisca. And the women, children, elderly have -- are being taken and dropped off here at the zone for them to walk into the free territory towards Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And does the investigation reveal that any able-bodied men were separated there?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That as well, as Tisca.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I note it says 12 or 13 July. How was it that you weren't able to identify which day it was?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they started the evacuation, deportation of the refugees, on the 12th and it continued into the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There's no way to distinguish exactly which date it was, I take it?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from this specific footage. I -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, let's -- I think we can play that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We've now come at 02.15.28.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's obviously a different film. But before I get to that, we saw the Muslim women and children and elderly walking down the main road. Do you know roughly -- and roughly just how long they had to walk before they got to the actual Muslim lines where they could be taken care of?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say between 5 and 10 kilometres. It might be 5 or 7 kilometres, but I'm not a hundred per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And now we -- we see the still of the next clip, which it also says 12 or 13 July, and it looks like it's a different footage. Can you tell us, first of all, the material before that, that was clear, of the people getting off the buses, where did that come from?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, that's the footage that we got from the BBC, which they got from WTN and Reuters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And how about this footage, this more blurry footage?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the blurry footage comes from Srpska Radio Television.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And they're now walking towards a camera. Can you tell, do you know where this camera is being shot from now, as opposed to the last one which was at their backs?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular still, particular shot, I'm -- I'm -- yeah, I don't know. I don't know if they're -- I mean, presumably they're closer to Kladanj, but I -- I can't tell from this where exactly they are located.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just play that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we see a person in camouflage on the left of the screen with a camouflage T-shirt on, and do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's Colonel Boering.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is seen in the Hotel Fontana footage that you would have seen earlier at the three different meetings, and he also testified in the Popovic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And do you -- we just saw some people in other camouflage uniforms going the other way, do you know, as we see other camouflage, who or what units will we begin to see, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We'll begin to see the Bosnian Muslim units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so where would that be?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Closer to the -- closer to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- let's just finish playing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Stop for a moment, please. Judge Mindua has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. McCloskey, I apologise, the video we have just seen, Luke, 12th or 13th of July, 1993 [as interpreted], the witness has said that she didn't know exactly when this footage was taken, since the evacuation lasted from the 12th to the 13th. So this is my question: Why did she not question or why did the investigators not question the people concerned or even the soldiers I see now on this still, as is the case for the other videos when she recognised or identified a number of people and when she said, We know who these people are, and we know on what date this happened? Why is this not the case for the previous video, 12th or 13th of July, 1993 [as interpreted], Luke, and we don't know when? And why is this the case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For the record, I'm quite sure that Judge Mindua is referring to 1995 and not to 1993 as he was recorded twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. I meant 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you perhaps answer this question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In some instances, the witnesses actually don't remember if it was the 12th or 13th, that it was one of those two days that they've stated, themselves. When we've had chances to go back and re-interview witnesses, sometimes we try to clarify that and are able to and other times not, so we're not able to, ourselves. In this particular footage of Luke, the only person that I believe was ever identified as being there is Colonel Boering. And I'd have to -- I'd have to refresh my recollection as to what he says, if it is -- if he's able to clarify that at all on the 12th or 13th. I'm presuming he wasn't able to because of the fact that it's titled the 12th or the 13th, but I actually don't know. I haven't interviewed him myself. I would be glad to double-check just to make sure if we can get any further as to which day that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, Colonel Boering will be a witness and will be able to assist on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But regarding the Judge's questions, the first clip that showed at the drop-off point on the Serb side, do you remember any people that were you able to even identify from that side?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was a -- a -- I don't know if he was a Major Sarkic who was at that point. Anything more -- I can't tell you much more about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if the Court doesn't object, I think another bit of homework is to review Major Sarkic, to see if he was able to distinguish or was ever asked that point. That might help answer Judge Mindua's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I think we can continue then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, if we could just stop it. 02.16.28.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We obviously had a change-over. Do you -- can you account for that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. This is now different footage, different source footage, of -- actually of a filmmaker from Norway for Norwegian TV who had done this -- this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is this the same exodus that we saw in the previous footage where we see Major Boering coming out with the refugees?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The first shot, it looked like it was at night. But now we see a big tunnel. Have you been to that tunnel?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Have you -- do you know about where such a tunnel would be?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, it would be between Tisca and Kladanj, but I don't know exactly where the tunnel is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We are now at 02.17.33.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Entitled "Tuzla Airport," again, 12 or 13 July 1995. Can you tell us where this footage came from?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you'll see it's a combination of, once again, news footage, as well as this Norwegian film-maker Maria Warsinski, who did a lot of this footage that we also got from Sarajevo TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, again, the investigation did not distinguish or was not able to distinguish between 12 and -- whether this was 12 or 13 July?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you just briefly remind us where Tuzla airport fits into this, just very briefly?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- it's where the refugees ultimately end up in camps, in the grounds near the Tuzla airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we stop for a moment. Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: I just want a clarification where exactly this video is, where these people are in the video that we are seeing now and a few minutes before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is near the Tuzla airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that's one place we didn't have time to go to, so can you help orient where Tuzla is? Let's start -- well, where they were dropped off, Vlasenica, the Court's much -- very familiar with, and from Vlasenica to Luke, the drop-offs point, roughly how many kilometres is that? Just give your best, rough -- or how long it took you to drive, if you've been there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Just before she answers, maybe you can also clarify in who -- in whose custody these people are at this point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At this point they've been let out of the buses, so they are now free. They're -- they have walked into Muslim territory. And so they're -- they're no longer in Bosnian Serb territory or custody. And in terms of the area, it's -- it's, you know, north-west of Srebrenica, west of Kladanj. And I wouldn't want to -- I've never driven -- I've driven to Tuzla many times but not that direct route, many different routes. So off the top of my head, I wouldn't want to guess how many kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We'll get a map up so you can visualize that. But just to make it clear, when they walk through that tunnel and come out to where those Bosnian Muslim soldiers are, is that -- what town area is that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would be approaching Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Kladanj, the town of Kladanj, is that a Muslim territory or Serb?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then if you go up to Tuzla, is -- Tuzla is what territory?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is also Muslim territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this large area where we see the Muslims, you've said Tuzla airport. Is that the Tuzla airport that we are seeing, that open area?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Where you see tents set up, the wire -- the barbed wire there, it's -- it's where they are placed for -- placed temporarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So we do see this barbed wire. I think there's indications of fences. Were they held in custody by anybody at this point?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
